sections.body:
### Symptom

A case needs a different owner, or an agent is trying to take a case they do not own.

### Checks

1. Confirm whether the case is owned by the asking user, in the L1 Support Queue, or in the L2 Escalation Queue.
2. Confirm L1 does not have Transfer Cases. Support Lead L2 does.
3. Confirm queue membership is the public group Support_L1 or Support_L2, not the permission set group.
4. Confirm a manual escalation still needs an escalation reason and Escalated By before the status can be Escalated.

### Resolution

1. If the case is in the L1 Support Queue and the user is in the public group Support_L1, they may take ownership from that queue.
2. If the case is owned by someone else and is not in that queue, L1 does not transfer it.
3. Ask Support Lead L2 to transfer it, or to take it from the L2 Escalation Queue.
4. Do not delete the case and recreate it to change the owner.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Support Lead L2 for any transfer L1 cannot perform. Escalate to Ops Admin when the user should be in the public group and is not.

### Symptom

A user cannot open Sales Dashboard or Support Dashboard, or the dashboard opens and looks empty.

### Checks

1. Use the same group check as report access. Without Run Reports, the user cannot open the dashboard. Public read-only folders do not override that.
2. Confirm the dashboard runs as the logged-in user. Pipeline By Stage shows that user's own opportunities. A Sales Rep should not expect the full-book 221,000 figure.
3. Confirm no synthetic load has been run. Empty charts are expected before that load. The metric notes still say the dashboard value was not observed.
4. Confirm the user is not L1 asking for Support Dashboard. L1 is not the audience.

### Resolution

1. For a missing Run Reports permission, follow the report-access resolution. Do not change the folder share from this page.
2. For an empty dashboard, confirm whether the user can see the underlying records. If they cannot, the chart is empty because of sharing, not because the dashboard failed.
3. Do not edit a dashboard component to force a number.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Support Lead L2 for a support-metric question, and to Ops Admin when a user with the correct group cannot open the dashboard at all.

### Symptom

A named user cannot log in to the Developer Edition org.

### Checks

1. Confirm the login host is https://login.salesforce.com. The sandbox host test.salesforce.com is not used. This project has no sandbox.
2. Confirm the username is that person's named user. Shared passwords are out of bounds.
3. Confirm the user is one of the two Salesforce CRM licenses, or a platform user that is actually assigned. Four personas are roles, not four simultaneous CRM logins.
4. Confirm you are not asking an L1 agent to reset another person's password. Manage Users is on the Ops Admin permission set only.

### Resolution

1. Retry the login at https://login.salesforce.com with the named username.
2. If the password is forgotten, stop. Ask the named Ops Admin to reset that user.
3. Do not create a shared login to get around a lockout.
4. Do not change a profile or a permission set from this page.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when the login host and username are correct and the user still cannot log in, or when both CRM users are locked out.

### Symptom

The user reaches the password step and the authenticator code is rejected, or the user has no verification method on this device.

### Checks

1. Confirm the device clock is correct. A skewed clock rejects a time-based code.
2. Confirm the user is enrolling their own method. Do not accept a code sent by chat from another person.
3. Confirm nobody is asking to turn MFA off for the org or for one user. This runbook has no approved bypass.

### Resolution

1. Ask the user to retry with the device time set automatically.
2. If the code still fails, stop. Do not invent a temporary code, a backup code, or a profile change.
3. Ask Ops Admin to review the user's verification method. Ops Admin does that in the org. This assistant cannot.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when a time check did not fix the code, or when anyone asks to disable MFA.

### Symptom

A list or report looks empty, or a record the user just created is not where they expected it.

### Checks

1. Confirm the list is filtered to the owner's records. A Sales Rep does not see another rep's opportunities.
2. Confirm the synthetic dataset has not been loaded. Empty orgs are expected. The hand counts in the metric notes apply only after that load.
3. Confirm the four flows are Draft. Lead Assignment and Case Assignment do not move the owner while they are Draft. The creator remains the owner.
4. Confirm nobody deleted the record to hide it. Sales Rep and L1 have no delete permission on their objects. L2 has no case delete.

### Resolution

1. Clear list filters and search by the record name the user saved.
2. If the record is owned by the creator, tell the user that routing has not run because the flow is Draft.
3. Do not load data, activate a flow, or delete rows from this page.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when a record was saved, the user has access to that object, and a name search still cannot find it.

### Symptom

A user cannot see a lead, opportunity, or case they expected to open.

### Checks

1. Confirm which persona group is assigned. Sales Rep has no case access. L1 has no lead or opportunity edit, and sees cases they own or that are in the L1 Support Queue. L2 can view all cases. Ops Admin can view all of the business objects.
2. Confirm the record owner and, for a case, whether it is in the L1 Support Queue or the L2 Escalation Queue.
3. Confirm User.Persona__c is only a Lightning label. It does not grant access. A blank persona does not make the user a Sales Rep or an agent.
4. The intended org-wide defaults are private for Lead, Opportunity, and Case, and public read only for Account and Contact. Those defaults are not deployed yet. Visibility today follows the permission set and the owner.

### Resolution

1. If the user should not see that object, explain the contract and stop. Do not grant View All or Modify All Data.
2. If the case should be in the L1 queue, confirm Ops Admin added the user to the public group Support_L1. The permission set group does not add queue membership.
3. If an L1 user needs a case they do not own and it is not in the L1 queue, they do not take it. Use case reassignment.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Support Lead L2 when the case is escalated or in the L2 queue. Escalate to Ops Admin when the permission set group or the public group is wrong.

### Symptom

A user cannot run a report, or an L1 agent is asking for the all-team case backlog.

### Checks

1. Confirm the permission set group. Sales Rep includes Run Reports through Reporting_Sales. Support Lead L2 includes Run Reports through Reporting_Support. Ops Admin includes report administration through Reporting_Admin. Support Agent L1 has no reporting permission set.
2. Confirm the report folder. Pipeline By Stage is the sales report scoped to the running user. Cases By Status is the L2 backlog, grouped by status and priority.
3. Confirm L1 is not a consumer of the all-team support report. That exclusion is the requirement, not a broken folder.

### Resolution

1. If the user is L1 and wants the team backlog, explain that L2 runs it. Do not add Run Reports to the L1 group.
2. If a Sales Rep or L2 user should have Run Reports and the group is missing, stop. Ops Admin assigns the group.
3. Do not clone the Ops Admin permission set to fix a missing report.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when a Sales Rep or Support Lead L2 has the correct group and still cannot run a report in their folder.

### Symptom

A record has a wrong field value, or a load did not match the synthetic counts.

### Checks

1. Confirm who may edit the field. Sales Rep edits own leads and opportunities. L1 edits own or queue cases, except Resolution Notes and Return Guidance, which are read-only. L2 edits cases and does not delete them. Ops Admin can edit the project fields, including Persona.
2. Confirm the correction is a new value on the field the validation message names, not a delete of the row.
3. For a synthetic load, confirm the order in the reporting notes. Leads that should convert are inserted as Qualified and converted without creating an extra opportunity. Closed Won amounts are greater than zero. Escalated cases need a reason and a real user in Escalated By. The flows stay Draft during the load.
4. Confirm two CRM users cannot own five logical owner names at once. Closed-by-agent groupings follow the real owner.

### Resolution

1. Ask the person who is allowed to edit the field to enter the corrected value and save.
2. Do not mass-delete leads, cases, or opportunities to make a chart match.
3. Do not convert the ten target leads if that convert will also create opportunities on top of the 18-row opportunity file.
4. This assistant does not edit the record.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when the correction needs a field the support user cannot edit, a delete, or a reload of the synthetic file.

### Symptom

A lead or case did not move as the user expected, or a fault message names Lead Assignment, Case Assignment, First Response Tracking, or Escalation.

### Checks

1. Confirm the flow status in source. All four flows are Draft. A Draft flow does not run.
2. Confirm which outcome the design uses. OwnerNotFound and QueueNotFound are handled outcomes, not faults. A fault is an unexpected failure while reading or updating a record.
3. For Escalation, confirm the design refuses to update when the L2 queue is missing or no active user has Persona Ops Admin. That refusal avoids a save that would break the escalation validation rule.
4. Confirm First Response Tracking stamps First Response At only when the prior status was New, the new status is not New, and the field is empty.

### Resolution

1. If the flow is Draft, tell the user the owner will stay the creator. Do not activate the flow from this page.
2. If a fault is reported after a future activation, copy the fault message and the flow name. Do not edit the flow in the org.
3. Leave the record as saved. Do not run a second update to hide the message.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when a flow is Active and was not activated under a release, or when a fault message appears. Ops Admin uses the release plan. This assistant does not deploy or activate anything.

### Symptom

A user can see the wrong objects, cannot run a report they should run, or was given setup access they should not have.

### Checks

1. Confirm the profile has no object permissions. Business access is on the permission set inside the group.
2. Confirm the group. Sales Rep contains Sales_Rep and Reporting_Sales. Support Agent L1 contains only Support_L1. Support Lead L2 contains Support_L2 and Reporting_Support. Ops Admin contains Ops_Admin and Reporting_Admin.
3. Confirm L1 has no Run Reports permission and no Transfer Cases permission. L2 has Transfer Cases and view-all cases, and no case delete. No set includes Modify All Data.
4. Confirm queue membership separately. The group does not add the user to Support_L1 or Support_L2.
5. Confirm User.Persona__c matches the story for Lightning. It is not the grant.

### Resolution

1. Tell the user which group matches the job. Do not assign it yourself unless you are the named Ops Admin.
2. Ops Admin assigns one group and sets Persona. Ops Admin does not grant Modify All Data to finish a ticket.
3. If an L1 user needs the team report, the answer is no. L2 runs that report.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when the assigned group does not match this table. Support Lead L2 does not manage users, profiles, or permission sets.

### Symptom

A promotion to Org B or Org A failed, a validation script failed after a deploy, or someone wants to skip UAT.

### Checks

1. Confirm which package it was. Release 1 is the operating process and access model. Release 2 is reports and dashboards and depends on Release 1.
2. Confirm the changelog outcome. Both releases are Not executed until a deploy id and commit SHA are written. Rollback status stays Not required until an org actually changed.
3. Confirm the path. Development is a scratch org. UAT is Org B. The production stand-in is Org A. There is no sandbox and no customer production org.
4. Confirm Flosum is Not Executed. A failed or missing Flosum login is not a release path.
5. Confirm whether Org B could be attached as a Lifecycle Center stage. That check has not been run. If it fails later, the same git commit is deployed with the CLI and the limitation is written down.

### Resolution

1. Stop the next stage. Do not merge to main and do not force push.
2. Record the commit SHA, the org alias, and the error text on the work item.
3. Re-run the validation script named on the work item. A skipped script is a failed promotion, not a reason to roll back.
4. Start the rollback drill only when a rollback criterion in the release plan is met. The drill is a tabletop until Ops Admin runs it. A normal deploy does not delete metadata. Removing Release 2 needs the destructive change list, and only after Org B accepts that removal.
5. Do not activate the four flows as part of recovering a failed deploy.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin for every release failure. Support Lead L2 does not approve production promotion and does not deploy.

### Symptom

A dashboard number does not match what a manager expected from the synthetic notes.

### Checks

1. Confirm the dashboard has been rendered. The metric notes say the dashboard value was not observed, because no org was connected when those notes were written.
2. Confirm the comparison only after the synthetic load. Open opportunity amount for a user who can read every opportunity is 221000 across 13 open rows. Conversion rate after the ten conversions is 41.67 percent, which is 10 divided by 24. Open cases are 15. Escalated cases are 4. Average first response on the 16 stamped cases is 3.00 hours.
3. Confirm who is looking. Pipeline By Stage is the running user's own opportunities. A Sales Rep must not be compared with the full-book 221000. In the file, Rep A owns 165000 of open amount and Rep B owns 56000.
4. Confirm the month. Opportunities Closing This Month is the current calendar month. The 11 opportunities and 212000 amount are a November 2026 run.
5. Confirm L1 is not the person judging the team dashboard.

### Resolution

1. If the viewer, the load, or the month explains the gap, tell the user the expected figure for that situation. Do not edit the report.
2. If the viewer can read every row, the load is complete, the month matches, and the number still differs, record the report name, the filter, and both numbers.
3. Do not change a formula, a filter, or a dashboard component in the org to force the hand count.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin when the documented conditions are met and the number still differs. Ops Admin treats a report change as a work item.

### Symptom

A save fails and Salesforce shows one of the six project rule messages.

### Checks

1. Lead, email or phone: Enter an email address or a phone number before saving this lead. Mobile does not count.
2. Lead convert: Convert this lead only when its status is Qualified. The convert action writes Closed - Converted. The rule looks at the status from before that write.
3. Closed Won: Enter an amount greater than zero before setting the stage to Closed Won. Closed Lost and open stages are not blocked for a blank amount.
4. Escalated case: Enter the escalation reason and the agent who escalated before saving an escalated case.
5. Closed case: Enter resolution notes before closing this case.
6. Return to L1: Enter return guidance before sending an escalated case back to L1. This applies when the prior status was Escalated and the new status is New, Working, or Waiting on Customer.

### Resolution

1. Read the message to the user and name the field to fill.
2. Ask the user to enter that value and save again. Do not deactivate the rule.
3. L1 cannot edit Resolution Notes or Return Guidance. If the task is a close or a return, Support Lead L2 enters those fields. L2 still cannot delete the case.

### Escalation Criteria

Escalate to Ops Admin only when the message does not match one of the six rules above, or when the approved process itself needs a change. That change is a work item, not an in-org edit.

Page: Sales Rep, task 3 of 4

### Steps

1. Open the opportunity you own.
2. For Closed Won, enter an amount greater than zero, then set the stage to Closed Won.
3. If Amount is blank, zero, or negative, the save stops with: Enter an amount greater than zero before setting the stage to Closed Won.
4. For Closed Lost, set the stage to Closed Lost. A blank amount is allowed on Closed Lost.
5. Update Next Step so the handoff or the loss is clear.

### Expected outcome

Closed Won is saved only with a positive amount. Closed Lost is saved without that amount check.

### Troubleshooting

- Do not put a zero amount on a won deal to make a forecast look smaller. The rule blocks it.
- Closed Won and Closed Lost are the only closed stages.

Page: Sales Rep, task 1 of 4

### Steps

1. Open a lead you own. You can create and edit your own leads. You cannot delete a lead.
2. Enter an email address or a phone number before you save. A mobile number does not satisfy the rule. If both are blank, the save stops with: Enter an email address or a phone number before saving this lead.
3. Set Product Interest to Core Product, Add-on Service, Renewal, or Undecided.
4. Use only these statuses: Open - Not Contacted, Working - Contacted, Qualified, Unqualified, and Closed - Converted. Closed - Converted is written by the convert action.
5. Set the status to Qualified only when the lead is ready to become an account, a contact, and an opportunity.
6. Convert from Qualified. The convert action sets Closed - Converted. If the prior status was anything else, the save stops with: Convert this lead only when its status is Qualified.

### Expected outcome

The lead becomes an account, a contact, and an opportunity through the standard convert action. You still have no access to cases.

### Troubleshooting

- Do not convert an Unqualified lead to remove it from the list. Leave it Unqualified.
- Lead Assignment is Draft. The owner stays the person who created the lead until Ops Admin activates that flow under a release. Do not expect a placeholder owner such as sales.core@org-ops.invalid to appear while the flow is Draft.
- Name and Company are still required by Salesforce. This page does not replace those standard requirements.

Page: Sales Rep quick reference

| Task | Do this | Stop when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lead | Email or phone, then Product Interest, then Qualified, then convert | The convert error names any status other than Qualified |
| Pipeline | Contract stage plus Next Step | You need a stage that is not on the path |
| Close | Positive amount, then Closed Won | Amount is blank, zero, or negative |
| Report | Pipeline By Stage, your own rows | You have no Run Reports permission |

### Expected outcome

You can pick the page that matches the task without opening setup.

### Troubleshooting

- If the task is not in the table, do not invent a click path. Ask Support or Ops Admin.
- You cannot delete leads or opportunities, edit cases, or change users, profiles, or permission sets.

Page: Sales Rep, task 4 of 4

### Steps

1. Confirm Ops Admin has assigned the Sales Rep permission set group. That group includes Run Reports. Your profile alone does not.
2. Open the Sales Leadership folder and run Pipeline By Stage.
3. Read the rows as your own opportunities. The report scope is the running user. Amount, close date, and next step are on the row.
4. Use Opportunities Closing This Month only as a leadership view of the current calendar month. Your own rows are the ones you can see.
5. Do not open the Support Leadership dashboard for case work. You have no case access, and that dashboard is not your job.

### Expected outcome

You can explain your own book by stage without an admin running the report for you.

### Troubleshooting

- If Run Reports is missing, stop. Ask Ops Admin to assign the Sales Rep group. Do not ask for the Ops Admin group.
- A full-book total such as 221,000 open amount is the Ops Admin figure, not the figure a single rep should expect.
- The four flows are Draft. Nothing on this page activates them.

Page: Sales Rep, task 2 of 4

### Steps

1. Open an opportunity you own. You can create, read, and edit your own opportunities. You cannot delete one.
2. Keep the stage on this path: Prospecting, Qualification, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed Won, Closed Lost.
3. Fill Next Step with the next action, in 255 characters or fewer.
4. Keep Amount and Close Date current when you know them. Open stages may be saved with Amount blank. Closed Lost may be saved with Amount blank.
5. Read Account and Contact for context. Do not try to edit a case from this page. You have no case access.

### Expected outcome

The opportunity shows a contract stage and a next step another person can read. Your pipeline report can group it by stage.

### Troubleshooting

- If the stage you want is not in the list, do not type a private stage. The value set is the contract path.
- Support Lead L2 can read the opportunity and Next Step is read-only for that persona. That does not change what you can edit on your own record.

Page: Support Agent, task 1 of 4

### Steps

1. Create a case. You can create, read, and edit cases you own or that sit in the L1 Support Queue. You cannot delete a case.
2. Leave status at New until you start work. New is the default.
3. Set Priority to Low, Medium, or High, and Origin to Phone, Email, or Web.
4. Set Type to Question, Problem, or Feature Request when you know it.
5. Link the contact and account when you know them. You can read accounts and contacts. You cannot edit leads or opportunities.
6. Add the working notes on the case. Do not keep the only copy in a side chat.

### Expected outcome

The request is a case with owner, status, priority, and origin. A brand-new case stays on New until the first working change.

### Troubleshooting

- Case Assignment is Draft. Creating a case does not yet route it to the L1 or L2 queue. The owner stays the creator until Ops Admin activates that flow under a release.
- If you cannot see a case you do not own and it is not in the L1 Support Queue, that is the access contract. Use the L1 record-visibility page in the runbook. Do not ask for View All Cases.

Page: Support Agent, task 3 of 4

### Steps

1. Open the case you own or that is in the L1 Support Queue.
2. Write the escalation reason in Escalation Reason.
3. Set Escalated By to yourself, the agent who is escalating.
4. Set status to Escalated.
5. If either the reason or Escalated By is blank, the save stops with: Enter the escalation reason and the agent who escalated before saving an escalated case.
6. Stop. You do not write Return Guidance or the final Resolution Notes. Those fields are read-only for L1. L2 writes them.

### Expected outcome

The case is Escalated, with a reason and the escalating agent stored on the record. L2 can see it.

### Troubleshooting

- Other statuses do not require the reason or Escalated By.
- The Escalation flow is Draft. It does not move the case to the L2 queue on a timer until Ops Admin activates it under a release. Your manual escalation is still valid.
- You cannot transfer a case you do not own. Transfer Cases is an L2 permission. Use the case-reassignment runbook page.

Page: Support Agent quick reference

| Task | Do this | Stop when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New request | Create a case on New, with priority and origin | You need to delete the case |
| First work | Leave New, once | First Response At already has a value |
| Escalate | Reason, Escalated By, then status Escalated | You are about to type resolution notes or return guidance |
| Someone else's case | Only if it is in the L1 Support Queue | It is owned by another person and not in your queue |

### Expected outcome

You can pick the page that matches the task without opening setup.

### Troubleshooting

- If the task is not in the table, do not invent a click path. Open the L1 runbook or escalate.
- You cannot run the team reports, transfer any case, or change users.

Page: Support Agent, task 2 of 4

### Steps

1. Open a case whose status is New and whose First Response At is empty.
2. Change the status from New to Working, Waiting on Customer, or another status that is not New. Do this when you first work the case.
3. Leave First Response At empty if it is empty. First Response Tracking stamps it once, when the status leaves New, and only if the field is still empty.
4. Save. Do not clear a time that is already stored. The flow does not overwrite it, and you should not try to.

### Expected outcome

The first time the case leaves New, First Response At receives the current date and time. A later status change does not replace that value.

### Troubleshooting

- The flow is Draft until a release activates it. While it is Draft, the field stays empty unless a person is allowed to set it. L1 can edit the field. Set it only when you are recording the real first response, and set it once.
- If the status was never New, the stamp does not apply. The skip path is for a case that was already past New.

Page: Support Agent, task 4 of 4

### Steps

1. Work only cases you own or cases in the L1 Support Queue.
2. Do not delete a case. The L1 permission set does not allow delete.
3. Do not edit a lead or an opportunity.
4. Do not run the Sales Leadership or Support Leadership reports. The L1 permission set group does not include Run Reports. The all-team backlog is an L2 report.
5. Do not assign permission sets, change profiles, or deploy a release. Those are Ops Admin actions.
6. When a limit blocks the task, stop and use the L1 runbook. If the runbook says to escalate, escalate to Support Lead L2 or Ops Admin as that page states.

### Expected outcome

L1 work stays on owned and queue cases. Setup, releases, and the all-team dashboard stay with the roles that have those permissions.

### Troubleshooting

- User.Persona__c does not grant access. A blank or wrong persona changes Lightning guidance. It does not give you cases, reports, or setup.
- Membership of the L1 Support Queue is the public group Support_L1. Assigning the permission set group does not add you to that public group. Ops Admin adds the user to the group.
